ctx.x: Okay, we were going to talk about how you came to make the record with Jelly Roll Morton in 1939.

Well, Jelly Roll lived at 207 West 131st Street, which I'm living at the same place now. And I was living at 2139 7th Avenue, which is on the corner of the next half a block from where Jelly lived, and at 209, next door to where Jelly was staying then, we used to do our rehearsing in there (unintelligible) bunch of us. And we'd go rehearse for these recordings.

ctx.x: Or did she marry after that? Yes.

She might have married a man after, you know how (unintelligible) show business is. Sometimes, you know, things like that happen just right, like with Jelly Roll. His wrote wife road after I was in California, and when Jelly Roll left New York (unintelligible) made these (unintelligible) recordings with him, he took his car and drove to California because his wife, his rich wife had a hotel out there, and this girl that was with him up to the time, years on the stage and all, she wasn't married to Jelly Charlie.
No. No. No, well, that was just the result of an affair.
